name: Azure virtual network flow logs
description: Azure Network Watcher virtual network flow logs: one JSON record per collection interval, holding many flow tuples grouped by the ACL and rule that evaluated them, each tuple a 5-tuple plus direction, state, encryption and throughput.
source: Microsoft Learn's Virtual Network Flow Logs page (the Log format and Sample log record sections); field names confirmed against the vendor's own published sample record as indexed.

feed.label: Azure virtual network flow logs
feed.description: Layer 4 IP flow records for a virtual network: the network security group or Virtual Network Manager rule that evaluated each flow, its 5-tuple, direction, lifecycle state, encryption status and packet/byte counts.

event_time.label: Record time
event_time.description: When Azure Network Watcher wrote this record, in UTC. Aggregates flow tuples collected over roughly the previous minute; later than any single flowTimestamp inside it.

flow_time.label: Flow tuple timestamp
flow_time.description: When one flow tuple inside the record occurred, distinct from the record's own publish time.

event_category.label: Record category
event_category.description: Which kind of Azure Monitor diagnostic record this is. Every virtual network flow log record carries the fixed value FlowLogFlowEvent in both the category and operationName columns.

flow_log_version.label: Flow log schema version
flow_log_version.description: The flow log record schema version; decides which fields and which flowTuples layout (13 comma fields) apply.

flow_log_id.label: FlowLog resource GUID
flow_log_id.description: The resource GUID of the FlowLog resource that produced this record.

flow_log_resource_id.label: FlowLog resource id
flow_log_resource_id.description: The ARM resource id of the FlowLog resource itself, under a Network Watcher's flowLogs collection.

target_resource_id.label: Target resource id
target_resource_id.description: The ARM resource id of the virtual network, subnet or NIC the FlowLog is attached to, whose traffic this record describes.

interface_mac.label: Interface MAC address
interface_mac.description: The MAC address of the network interface where Azure captured the flow, written as 12 hex characters with no separators.

acl_id.label: Evaluating ACL id
acl_id.description: The id of the network security group or Azure Virtual Network Manager security-admin configuration that evaluated this traffic.

rule_name.label: Rule name
rule_name.description: The name of the NSG or Virtual Network Manager rule that allowed or denied the traffic; can also be a platform-generated name for traffic the Azure platform itself handled.

source_ip.label: Source address
source_ip.description: The address the flow's packets carried as the source.

dest_ip.label: Destination address
dest_ip.description: The address the flow's packets carried as the destination.

source_port.label: Source port
source_port.description: The source transport-layer port of the flow.

dest_port.label: Destination port
dest_port.description: The destination transport-layer port of the flow, usually the more useful of the pair for spotting a service.

protocol.label: Protocol
protocol.description: The flow's Layer 4 protocol, an IANA protocol number.

flow_direction.label: Flow direction
flow_direction.description: Whether the flow was inbound or outbound through the monitored interface.

flow_state.label: Flow state
flow_state.description: The tuple's position in the flow's lifecycle: begin, continuing, end or deny.

flow_encryption.label: Flow encryption status
flow_encryption.description: Whether the platform encrypted this flow and, if not, why.

packets_sent.label: Packets sent
packets_sent.description: Packets sent from source to destination since the tuple's last update.

bytes_sent.label: Bytes sent
bytes_sent.description: Packet bytes (header and payload) sent from source to destination since the tuple's last update.

packets_received.label: Packets received
packets_received.description: Packets sent from destination to source since the tuple's last update.

bytes_received.label: Bytes received
bytes_received.description: Packet bytes (header and payload) sent from destination to source since the tuple's last update.

mscs:vnet:flow.description: Azure virtual network flow logs as indexed in the dev Splunk: one event per flow log record, the records[] wrapper stripped at index time.
mscs:vnet:flow.note: flowRecords.flows{} and its flowGroups{} nest an array of ACLs and an array of rules per ACL; flowTuples{} nests one object per flow tuple. The vendor's own wire format documents each tuple as a 13-field comma-separated string (Log format section); this dev index instead holds one JSON object per tuple with the same 13 fields, named. Whether a production TA lands the comma string as-is (needing a delimited-field transform to reach these names) or reshapes it the same way was not found in this repository.

tuple_time_order.text: The record's own time is publish time, not event time: Azure batches roughly a minute of flow tuples before writing the record, so every flowTimestamp inside can be up to about 60 seconds earlier than the record's time.

guid_lookalikes.text: flowLogGUID (the FlowLog resource itself) and aclID (the NSG or Virtual Network Manager config evaluating the traffic) are both bare GUIDs with nothing in the string to tell them apart out of context.

lookalike_resource_ids.text: flowLogResourceID (the FlowLog resource) and targetResourceID (the resource the FlowLog watches) are both full ARM resource id strings and easy to swap; the sample record even cases them differently (upper-case SUBSCRIPTIONS/RESOURCEGROUPS on one, lower-case on the other), so a case-sensitive join can silently miss.

mac_no_separators.text: macAddress is 12 hex characters with no colons or dashes (112233445566); normalise before comparing to a colon-separated MAC from another source.

aggregate_counts.text: Continuing (C) and End (E) tuples carry packet and byte counts aggregated since the flow's previous tuple, not the flow's running total. Begin (B) tuples carry zero counts in the vendor's own sample record, though the vendor's separate bandwidth-calculation example shows a Begin tuple with the four count fields empty instead of zero.
